items.title: Authority to Execute Growing Canada’s Community Canopies – Urban
notes: Forestry Plans and Studies Grant Agreement
Report from Lucas Rogerson, Manager of Parks
Adam Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services provided an update on the grant application for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Growing Canada’s Community Canopies Grant program.

He noted that the approved grant funding of $89,160 will help strengthen and better manage the Township's urban canopy. The funding will also support the development of a detailed inventory of the Township's urban tree system and canopy, which will be incorporated into the Township's Natural Asset Management Program.
A. Gilmore responded to comments and questions from Council regarding the grant project and funding new tree projects.

items.title: Request for Tender #48-26: Asphalting of Various Roads - 2026
notes: Report from Sandi Wiles, Purchasing and Risk Supervisor Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer provided a report regarding the asphalting of various roads within the Township. He noted the RFT was issued in accordance with the Township’s purchasing and procurement by-law, the Township received three responses, and the successful vender is based on the lowest cost compliant bid.
A. Gilmore responded to comments and questions from Council regarding the Jefferson Elora Community Centre parking lot.

C. Baker responded to comments and questions from Council regarding section 13 Bridge Street and Tower St. asphalt replacement, stop blocks, accessible parking spaces, line painting, priority rehab and replacement, the Fergus Curling Club parking lot and BDT lifecycle.

items.title: RFP#28-26 Community Services Fee Study
notes: Report from Samoya Smith, Manager of Purchasing and Risk Adam McNabb, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer presented a report providing recommendations regarding fees and charges associated with Community Services programs, facility rentals, and related services. He noted an invitational RFP was issued to three vendors, and one submission was received.
A. McNabb responded to questions from Council regarding the RFP process and expanded search.
A. Gilmore responded to questions from Council regarding subsidy for equity deserving groups within the community and community engagement.
D. Wilson responded to comments and questions from council regarding expanded scope of the fee study, staffing, procurement process and engagement.

items.title: Lease of Office Space, 8460 Wellington Rd 19, Belwood
notes: Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided a report advising that, in June 2023, Council approved a lease agreement between the Township and the existing Postmaster for the lease of a portion of 8460 Wellington Road 19, Belwood, to facilitate the operation of a post office serving the Belwood area. Recently, Township staff were notified that the Postmaster will be retiring and has provided notice to terminate the lease for 8460 Wellington Road 19, Belwood, effective October 1, 2026.
D. Wilson responded to comments from Council regarding Canada Post’s long-term vision for the community of Belwood.

items.title: Councillor Wilton - Data Centres
notes: Given the rapid growth of AI-driven systems, cloud computing and digital infrastructure has accelerated the development of new and large-scale data centres to meet industry defined needs and the fact that the Province of Ontario has not yet established a provincial regulatory framework for AI data centre industry there is cause to exercise caution regarding the introduction of data centres within the Township of Centre Wellington.

1) Therefore the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington directs staff to undertake a review and study costing no more than $49,999 (of staff time) of the Township’s land use planning policies in relation to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, pursuant to section 38 of the Planning Act, applicable to all zones where the use is permitted in the Township of Centre Wellington, including, but not limited to, its Official Plans and Zoning By-law, and any required changes to the Township’s land use planning policies, mapping, and regulatory framework with consideration of, but not limited to the following:
a) Existing Official Plan policies and Zoning By-law permissions and regulations;
b) Energy use and the impacts to power grids,
c) Water use and the impacts to long term drinking water quality and quantity, and
d) Noise and light pollution impacts,
2) That staff be directed to report back to Council on the items listed above (a) in Q3 of 2027.

3) That staff be directed to prepare for Council’s consideration at the Council meeting on September 28, 2026, an Interim Control By-Law under Section 38 of the Planning Act, prohibiting the use of AI data centres within the study area described in (a) above.
